# Set Up
```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Current working directory
project_dir = Path.cwd()

# Move up one directory to Final Project
project_root = project_dir.parent

# Data directory
data_dir = project_root / "Datacollection"

# Define data folders
boundary_dir = data_dir / "roman_boundaries"
settlement_dir = data_dir / "roman_cities"

print("Working directory:", project_dir)
print("Project root:", project_root)
print("Data directory:", data_dir)

# Load settlement data
settlements_gdf = gpd.read_file(
    settlement_dir / "pleiades_settlements.geojson"
)

# Load battle-location links
battle_locations_df = pd.read_csv(
    data_dir / "roman_battle_location_links.csv"
)

print("Battle-location records:", len(battle_locations_df))
print(battle_locations_df.columns.tolist())



```


# Battles

## Set Up
```{python}
# Convert location coordinates to numeric values
battle_locations_df["location_latitude"] = pd.to_numeric(
    battle_locations_df["location_latitude"],
    errors="coerce"
)

battle_locations_df["location_longitude"] = pd.to_numeric(
    battle_locations_df["location_longitude"],
    errors="coerce"
)

# Remove records without valid coordinates
battle_locations_mapped = battle_locations_df.dropna(
    subset=["location_latitude", "location_longitude"]
).copy()

# Create GeoDataFrame
battle_locations_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    battle_locations_mapped,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(
        battle_locations_mapped["location_longitude"],
        battle_locations_mapped["location_latitude"]
    ),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)

print("Total battle-location records:", len(battle_locations_df))
print("Records with coordinates:", len(battle_locations_gdf))
print("Unique battles mapped:", battle_locations_gdf["battle_wikidata_id"].nunique())


```

# Settlements

## Set Up

```{python}
# Check the settlement coordinate reference system
print("Original CRS:", settlements_gdf.crs)

# Convert to WGS84 if necessary
if settlements_gdf.crs is not None:
    settlements_gdf = settlements_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

# Keep valid, non-empty point geometries
settlements_gdf = settlements_gdf[
    settlements_gdf.geometry.notna()
    & settlements_gdf.geometry.geom_type.eq("Point")
    & settlements_gdf.geometry.is_valid
    & ~settlements_gdf.geometry.is_empty
].copy()

print("Settlement records mapped:", len(settlements_gdf))
```

# Roman Boundaries

## Set Up

```{python}
# Find all boundary GeoJSON files
boundary_files = sorted(boundary_dir.glob("*.geojson"))

print("Boundary files found:", len(boundary_files))

# Load each boundary into a dictionary
boundaries = {}

for boundary_file in boundary_files:

    # Use filename as the dictionary key
    boundary_name = boundary_file.stem

    # Read GeoJSON
    boundary_gdf = gpd.read_file(boundary_file)

    # Store in dictionary
    boundaries[boundary_name] = boundary_gdf

    print(
        boundary_name,
        "| Records:", len(boundary_gdf),
        "| CRS:", boundary_gdf.crs,
        "| Geometry:", boundary_gdf.geom_type.unique()
    )

# Display the names of all loaded boundaries
print(boundaries.keys())
print("Total boundaries loaded:", len(boundaries))
```

## Individual Boundary Maps

```{python}
# Loop through each historical boundary
for boundary_name, boundary_gdf in boundaries.items():

    # Convert to WGS84
    if boundary_gdf.crs is not None:
        boundary_gdf = boundary_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    # Create map
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

    boundary_gdf.plot(
        ax=ax,
        facecolor="#D9E2EC",
        edgecolor="#041E42",
        linewidth=1
    )

    ax.set_title(
        f"Roman Empire: {boundary_name}",
        fontsize=16
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
    ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

```

# Battle Assigned to Appropriate Maps

```{python}
# Inspect battle dates
print(battle_locations_df["battle_date"].head(15))

print("\nData type:")
print(battle_locations_df["battle_date"].dtype)

```

## Set the Years

```{python}
# Extract signed year from Wikidata date
battle_locations_gdf["battle_year"] = (
    battle_locations_gdf["battle_date"]
    .str.extract(r"^([+-]\d{4})")[0]
    .astype(float)
)

# Inspect converted dates
print(
    battle_locations_gdf[
        ["battle_name", "battle_date", "battle_year"]
    ].head(15)
)

```

## Partition Them 
```{python}
# Define chronological boundary intervals
periods = [
    ("roman_264_BC", None, -264),
    ("roman_133_BC", -264, -133),
    ("roman_60_BC", -133, -60),
    ("roman_44_BC", -60, -44),
    ("roman_14_AD", -44, 14),
    ("roman_69_AD", 14, 69),
    ("roman_117_AD", 69, 117),
    ("roman_200_AD", 117, 200),
    ("roman_314_AD", 200, 314)
]

# Assign each battle to a period
def assign_period(year):

    for boundary_name, start_year, end_year in periods:

        if start_year is None and year <= end_year:
            return boundary_name

        elif start_year is not None and start_year < year <= end_year:
            return boundary_name

    return None


battle_locations_gdf["boundary_period"] = (
    battle_locations_gdf["battle_year"].apply(assign_period)
)

```

## Distribution
```{python}
# Count unique battles assigned to each period
for boundary_name, start_year, end_year in periods:

    period_battles = battle_locations_gdf[
        battle_locations_gdf["boundary_period"] == boundary_name
    ]

    print(
        boundary_name,
        "| Battle-location records:", len(period_battles),
        "| Unique battles:", period_battles["battle_wikidata_id"].nunique()
    )

# Check battles outside our six periods
unassigned = battle_locations_gdf[
    battle_locations_gdf["boundary_period"].isna()
]

print("\nUnassigned records:", len(unassigned))
print(
    "Unique unassigned battles:",
    unassigned["battle_wikidata_id"].nunique()
)

```

## Generate the Maps
```{python}
# Generate one map for each historical period
for boundary_name, start_year, end_year in periods:

    # Get corresponding Roman boundary
    boundary_gdf = boundaries[boundary_name].copy()

    # Convert boundary to WGS84
    if boundary_gdf.crs is not None:
        boundary_gdf = boundary_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    # Filter battles for this period
    period_battles = battle_locations_gdf[
        battle_locations_gdf["boundary_period"] == boundary_name
    ].copy()

    # Create map
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

    # Plot Roman territory
    boundary_gdf.plot(
        ax=ax,
        facecolor="#D9E2EC",
        edgecolor="#041E42",
        linewidth=1,
        alpha=0.8
    )

    # Plot battles
    if not period_battles.empty:
        period_battles.plot(
            ax=ax,
            color="#B23A48",
            markersize=12,
            alpha=0.65,
            label="Battle-associated locations"
        )

    # Format map
    ax.set_title(
        f"Battle-Associated Locations and Roman Territory: "
        f"{boundary_name}",
        fontsize=16
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
    ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")

    ax.legend(loc="lower left")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    print(
        boundary_name,
        "| Unique battles:",
        period_battles["battle_wikidata_id"].nunique()
    )

```

## Partitioning Settlements to fit on appropriate maps

### Set up
```{python}
# Convert settlement date fields to numeric values
settlements_gdf["MINDATE"] = pd.to_numeric(
    settlements_gdf["MINDATE"],
    errors="coerce"
)

settlements_gdf["MAXDATE"] = pd.to_numeric(
    settlements_gdf["MAXDATE"],
    errors="coerce"
)

# Keep settlements with valid date ranges
settlements_dated = settlements_gdf[
    settlements_gdf["MINDATE"].notna()
    & settlements_gdf["MAXDATE"].notna()
    & (settlements_gdf["MINDATE"] <= settlements_gdf["MAXDATE"])
].copy()

print("Total settlement records:", len(settlements_gdf))
print("Settlements with valid date ranges:", len(settlements_dated))
print(
    "Settlements without valid date ranges:",
    len(settlements_gdf) - len(settlements_dated)
)

# Inspect the converted dates
print(
    settlements_dated[
        ["ID", "GEOCONTEXT", "MINDATE", "MAXDATE"]
    ].head(15)
)

```

### Partitioning
```{python}
# Generate one settlement subset for each historical period
settlement_periods = {}

for boundary_name, start_year, end_year in periods:

    # Settlement must have begun by the end of the period
    period_settlements = settlements_dated[
        settlements_dated["MINDATE"] <= end_year
    ].copy()

    # Settlement must also potentially have existed after the start
    if start_year is not None:
        period_settlements = period_settlements[
            period_settlements["MAXDATE"] >= start_year
        ].copy()

    # Store settlements for this period
    settlement_periods[boundary_name] = period_settlements

    print(
        boundary_name,
        "| Settlements:", len(period_settlements)
    )

```


```{python}
# Generate one settlement map for each historical period
for boundary_name, start_year, end_year in periods:

    # Get corresponding Roman boundary
    boundary_gdf = boundaries[boundary_name].copy()

    # Convert boundary to WGS84
    if boundary_gdf.crs is not None:
        boundary_gdf = boundary_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    # Get settlements for this period
    period_settlements = settlement_periods[boundary_name]

    # Create map
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

    # Plot Roman territory
    boundary_gdf.plot(
        ax=ax,
        facecolor="#D9E2EC",
        edgecolor="#041E42",
        linewidth=1,
        alpha=0.8
    )

    # Plot settlements
    if not period_settlements.empty:
        period_settlements.plot(
            ax=ax,
            color="#2878A5",
            markersize=5,
            alpha=0.5,
            label="Ancient settlements"
        )

    # Format map
    ax.set_title(
        f"Ancient Settlements and Roman Territory: "
        f"{boundary_name}",
        fontsize=16
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
    ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")

    if not period_settlements.empty:
        ax.legend(loc="lower left")

    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    print(
        boundary_name,
        "| Settlements:",
        len(period_settlements)
    )


```

# Settlement Deep Dive


```{python}
# Inspect all settlement attributes
print("Number of settlement records:", len(settlements_gdf))

for column in settlements_gdf.columns:

    # Count non-null values
    non_null = settlements_gdf[column].notna().sum()

    # Count distinct values
    unique = settlements_gdf[column].nunique()

    # Calculate percentage populated
    percentage = round(non_null / len(settlements_gdf) * 100, 2)

    print(

        "| Non-null:", non_null,
        "| Unique:", unique,
        "| Populated:", f"{percentage}%"
    )
```

### Feature Investigation

```{python}
# Define feature categories to investigate
feature_categories = [
    "port",
    "temple",
    "fort",
    "amphitheatre",
    "theatre",
    "bath",
    "villa",
    "cemetery",
    "mine",
    "church"
]

# Count records containing each feature classification
for category in feature_categories:

    matching = settlements_gdf[
        settlements_gdf["FEATURETYP"]
        .str.contains(category, case=False, na=False)
    ]

    print(
        category,
        "| Records:", len(matching),
        "| Percentage:", round(
            len(matching) / len(settlements_gdf) * 100, 2
        )
    )

```


```{python}
# Define feature categories
feature_categories = [
    "port",
    "temple",
    "fort",
    "amphitheatre",
    "theatre"
]

# Create a summary table
feature_period_counts = []

for boundary_name, period_settlements in settlement_periods.items():

    for category in feature_categories:

        matching = period_settlements[
            period_settlements["FEATURETYP"]
            .str.contains(category, case=False, na=False)
        ]

        feature_period_counts.append({
            "period": boundary_name,
            "feature": category,
            "count": len(matching)
        })

# Convert results to DataFrame
feature_period_df = pd.DataFrame(feature_period_counts)

# Display counts by period
feature_period_pivot = feature_period_df.pivot(
    index="feature",
    columns="period",
    values="count"
)

feature_period_pivot

```

### Map all five feature types on the latest Roman boundary

```{python}
boundary_314 = boundaries["roman_314_AD"].copy()

if boundary_314.crs is not None:
    boundary_314 = boundary_314.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    ax=ax,
    facecolor="#E6E6E6",

)
```

## Partition the maps by historical period

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    3,
    3,
    figsize=(20, 16)
)

axes = axes.flatten()

for ax, (boundary_name, start_year, end_year) in zip(axes, periods):

    # Get the corresponding boundary
    boundary = boundaries[boundary_name].copy()

    if boundary.crs is not None:
        boundary = boundary.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    # Get settlements overlapping this period
    period_settlements = settlement_periods[boundary_name]

    # Plot the Roman boundary
    boundary.plot(
        ax=ax,
        facecolor="#E6E6E6",
        edgecolor="#041E42",
        linewidth=0.8,

    )

    # Plot each feature type

                case=False,
                na=False
            )
        ]

            ax=ax,
            marker=style["marker"],
            color=style["color"],
            markersize=12,
            alpha=0.75,

# Create one shared legend
```

# Combined Maps

## All Points on Latest Roman Map
```{python}
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Get the latest Roman boundary
boundary_314 = boundaries["roman_314_AD"].copy()

if boundary_314.crs is not None:
    boundary_314 = boundary_314.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

# Create the map
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Plot Roman territory
boundary_314.plot(
    ax=ax,
    facecolor="#E6E6E6",
    edgecolor="#041E42",
    linewidth=1,
    alpha=0.7
)

# 2. Plot all ancient settlements as small background points
settlements_gdf.plot(
    ax=ax,
    color="#9A9A9A",
    markersize=3,
    alpha=0.25,
    zorder=2
)

# 3. Plot special settlement features
for feature, style in feature_styles.items():

    feature_settlements = settlements_gdf[
        settlements_gdf["FEATURETYP"].str.contains(
            feature,
            case=False,
            na=False
        )
    ]

    if not feature_settlements.empty:
        feature_settlements.plot(
            ax=ax,
            marker=style["marker"],
            color=style["color"],
            markersize=22,
            alpha=0.85,
            edgecolor="black",
            linewidth=0.4,
            zorder=3
        )

# 4. Plot battle-associated locations
battle_locations_gdf.plot(
    ax=ax,
    marker="*",
    color="#B23A48",
    markersize=65,
    alpha=0.85,
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=0.4,
    zorder=4
)

# Create a custom legend
legend_elements = [
    Line2D(
        [0], [0],
        marker="o",
        color="w",
        markerfacecolor="#9A9A9A",
        markersize=5,
        label="Other ancient settlements"
    ),
    Line2D(
        [0], [0],
        marker="*",
        color="w",
        markerfacecolor="#B23A48",
        markeredgecolor="black",
        markersize=13,
        label="Battle-associated locations"
    )
]

# Add the five special settlement types
for feature, style in feature_styles.items():

    legend_elements.append(
        Line2D(
            [0], [0],
            marker=style["marker"],
            color="w",
            markerfacecolor=style["color"],
            markeredgecolor="black",
            markersize=9,
            label=feature.capitalize()
        )
    )

ax.set_title(
    "Roman Battles and Ancient Settlements "
    "within the Roman Territorial Extent (314 AD)",
    fontsize=17,
    pad=15
)

ax.legend(
    handles=legend_elements,
    title="Map Features",
    loc="lower left",
    fontsize=10
)

ax.set_axis_off()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


```


## Partitioned Map

```{python}
# Create a 3 x 3 grid of maps
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    3,
    3,
    figsize=(22, 17)
)

axes = axes.flatten()

# Generate one map for each historical period
for ax, (boundary_name, start_year, end_year) in zip(axes, periods):

    # Get the corresponding Roman boundary
    boundary = boundaries[boundary_name].copy()

    if boundary.crs is not None:
        boundary = boundary.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    # Get settlements overlapping this historical period
    period_settlements = settlement_periods[boundary_name]

    # Get battles assigned to this historical period
    period_battles = battle_locations_gdf[
        battle_locations_gdf["boundary_period"] == boundary_name
    ].copy()

    # 1. Plot Roman territory
    boundary.plot(
        ax=ax,
        facecolor="#E6E6E6",
        edgecolor="#041E42",
        linewidth=0.8,
        alpha=0.7,
        zorder=1
    )

    # 2. Plot all settlements as background points
    if not period_settlements.empty:

        period_settlements.plot(
            ax=ax,
            color="#9A9A9A",
            markersize=2,
            alpha=0.2,
            zorder=2
        )

    # 3. Plot special settlement features
    for feature, style in feature_styles.items():

        feature_settlements = period_settlements[
            period_settlements["FEATURETYP"].str.contains(
                feature,
                case=False,
                na=False
            )
        ]

        if not feature_settlements.empty:

            feature_settlements.plot(
                ax=ax,
                marker=style["marker"],
                color=style["color"],
                markersize=12,
                alpha=0.85,
                edgecolor="black",
                linewidth=0.2,
                zorder=3
            )

    # 4. Plot battle-associated locations
    if not period_battles.empty:

        period_battles.plot(
            ax=ax,
            marker="*",
            color="#B23A48",
            markersize=35,
            alpha=0.85,
            edgecolor="black",
            linewidth=0.3,
            zorder=4
        )

    # Count unique battles for the panel title
    battle_count = period_battles["battle_wikidata_id"].nunique()

    # Format panel title
    period_title = (
        boundary_name
        .replace("roman_", "")
        .replace("_", " ")
    )

    ax.set_title(
        f"{period_title}\n"
        f"{battle_count} battles | "
        f"{len(period_settlements)} settlements",
        fontsize=12
    )

    ax.set_axis_off()


# Create a shared legend
legend_elements = [
    Line2D(
        [0], [0],
        marker="o",
        color="w",
        markerfacecolor="#9A9A9A",
        markersize=5,
        label="Other ancient settlements"
    ),
    Line2D(
        [0], [0],
        marker="*",
        color="w",
        markerfacecolor="#B23A48",
        markeredgecolor="black",
        markersize=12,
        label="Battle-associated locations"
    )
]

# Add special settlement categories
for feature, style in feature_styles.items():

    legend_elements.append(
        Line2D(
            [0], [0],
            marker=style["marker"],
            color="w",
            markerfacecolor=style["color"],
            markeredgecolor="black",
            markersize=9,
            label=feature.capitalize()
        )
    )


fig.legend(
    handles=legend_elements,
    title="Map Features",
    loc="lower center",
    ncol=7,
    fontsize=10,
    title_fontsize=11
)

fig.suptitle(
    "Roman Battles and Ancient Settlements Across Historical Periods",
    fontsize=19,
    y=0.98
)

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.07, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()

```
